title: Subnet role mapper and dynamic route tailoring Terraform module for private VPC deployments
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that implements subnet role mapping (control/compute/data), per-role route table generation, and dynamic egress routing with active health checks for NAT/IGW endpoints. The goal is a single module teams can plug into Private (VPC) deployments that enforces predictable egress patterns, supports multi-AZ failover, provides deterministic route priorities, and emits observability hooks used by the Console and runtime autoscaler.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Module accepts a declarative mapping of subnet CIDRs to roles (e.g., control, inference, storage) and produces separate route tables per role.
2) NAT Gateways (or managed NAT instances) are provisioned per-AZ for roles that require outbound internet; IGW is optional and only attached to public role subnets.
3) VPC endpoints (S3, ECR, STS, KMS) can be enabled per-role via a boolean map and produce correct endpoint route propagation.
4) Active health checks: the module deploys a small synthetic probe (Lambda or compute instance) that validates NAT reachability and marks a Route 53 health check/route preference which the module uses to switch routes to healthy egress paths.
5) Failover behavior: unhealthy NAT in one AZ causes route table updates to prefer healthy NATs in the same AZ, falling back to cross-AZ NAT only when allowed by config.
6) Multi-AZ idempotency: module can be safely re-run across AZ additions/removals with minimal manual state changes.
7) Outputs include route table IDs per role, NAT ids, endpoint ids, a human-readable upgrade plan snippet, and tags for Console ingestion.
8) Terraform registry-style examples and Terratest/CI coverage exist.
9) Documented upgrade path for replacing single shared NAT Gateway with per-AZ scaled NAT architecture without downtime.
implementation_notes: Design choices and tradeoffs: prefer managed NAT Gateways for reliability but allow opt-in for lower-cost NAT instances for dev accounts. Health probes should be optional and pluggable (customer-owned probe function). Use terraform state locking and migration scripts to remap route table associations during upgrades. Keep provider usage AWS-only for v1 but expose interface to add GCP/Azure later. Avoid hard-coding AZ names; rely on AZ index ordering. Tag all created resources with module provenance tags for easier cleanup and Console mapping.
tasks: Proto: implement subnet_role variable and generate route tables per role
Provision NAT per-AZ with configurable allocation strategy (shared vs per-az)
Implement optional IGW for public role and ensure correct default routes
Add VPC endpoint creation per-role with policy/document toggles
Health check submodule: lambda probe + CloudWatch metric + Route53 health check integration
Failover logic via route table association updates and prioritized static routes
Upgrade scripts: terraform import helpers and state move examples
Add Terratest integration and CI pipeline tests for AZ failover and endpoint connectivity
Write README with variables, example stacks, and upgrade cookbook
Prepare RFC and Confluence doc linking module design and rollback guidance
